questions.q: Define situational irony and give one example from the story where the actual outcome is the opposite of what the characters expect.
questions.a: Situational irony occurs when events turn out contrary to what is expected or appropriate. In the story, the son and daughter-in-law expect the old man to be grateful for their "care," but their actions (locking him out, taking his stick) actually strip him of dignity — the opposite of care. A wrong answer that only gives a dictionary definition without a story-specific example shows the student cannot apply the concept to the text.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the walking stick (गेसाई) functions as a symbol in the story. What does it represent beyond its physical use?
questions.a: The walking stick symbolizes the old man's self-respect, his lifelong labor, and his quiet resistance. It is not merely a support for walking; it carries the weight of his memories (the notches he carved), his authority (he used it to manage the fields), and his dignity (he refuses to let it be taken). A wrong answer that describes it only as a physical aid for walking reveals the student misses the symbolic layer and treats objects only literally.

questions.q: Identify one instance of verbal irony in the dialogue between the son (तेजपाल) and the old man (लव्ज़नकल). Quote the line (or paraphrase) and explain why it is ironic.
questions.a: When the son says, "पिता जी, आप आराम करो, हम आपकी सेवा करेंगे" (Father, you rest, we will serve you), but immediately locks him out and takes his stick, his words mean the opposite of his actions — that is verbal irony. The student must pinpoint the gap between spoken words and true intent. A wrong answer that picks a non-ironic line (e.g., a factual statement) shows confusion between verbal irony and simple dialogue.

questions.q: Compare the symbolic meaning of the bundle (पोटली) and the axe (फकसी) in the story. How do they represent opposing forces in the old man's life?
questions.a: The bundle represents the old man's past, memories, and the fragile possessions he clings to (his identity), while the axe represents the son's brutal practicality and the force that severs the old man's ties to his land and authority. Together they symbolize the conflict between sentimental continuity and ruthless displacement. A wrong answer that treats both as mere plot objects (e.g., "he carried a bundle, he used an axe") fails to analyze their thematic opposition.

questions.q: Evaluate the author's use of dramatic irony in the scene where the villagers watch the old man's humiliation. Why is the reader's awareness more painful than the characters'?
questions.a: The reader knows the old man's lifelong sacrifices (shown through flashbacks) while the villagers and son see only a burdensome old man; this gap makes the reader feel the injustice more acutely because we hold the full truth that the characters ignore. A wrong answer that says "it makes the story sad" without linking to the knowledge gap shows superficial evaluation.

questions.q: Write a short paragraph (4-5 lines) from the perspective of the walking stick, describing its journey from the old man's strong hand to the moment it is thrown aside. Use symbolism to show its feelings.
questions.a: A strong response will personify the stick, reference specific moments (carving notches, supporting the old man, being snatched), and convey the stick's symbolic role as a witness to dignity and betrayal. A poor answer will write a factual summary without personification or symbolic depth, indicating the student cannot creatively extend the symbol.
